blurb: The King of Terriers, the largest terrier, from Yorkshire's Aire valley
description: The Airedale Terrier is the largest terrier breed, from Yorkshire, England, with a wiry black and tan coat and an intelligent, independent, loyal temperament.
answer: The Airedale Terrier is the largest of the terrier breeds and comes from the valley of the River Aire in Yorkshire, England. It typically stands about 56 to 61 cm tall and weighs around 19 to 25 kg. It is commonly described as intelligent, independent, loyal and sometimes stubborn.

body: In the mid-19th century, working-class people in Airedale crossed the old English Black and Tan Terrier with the Otterhound and other breeds to create a versatile hunting and farm dog. Shown under names such as Bingley and Waterside Terrier, it was named the Airedale Terrier in 1879, a name the Kennel Club accepted in 1886. The AKC recognized it in 1888. Airedales carried messages and found wounded soldiers in World War I and were early police dogs in Britain. In the 1920s the Airedale was the most popular breed in the United States.

The Airedale has a hard, wiry broken coat with a softer undercoat, usually a black or grizzle saddle with a tan head, ears and legs. The tail is traditionally carried high. Larger Oorang-type Airedales, developed in Ohio in the 1920s, can reach much greater weights but usually do poorly in conformation shows. The coat is often called hypoallergenic, but studies have not found significantly lower allergen levels than in other dogs.

Bred to hunt independently, the Airedale is described as very intelligent, independent, strong-minded, stoic and sometimes stubborn, and very loyal to its owners. It is often called alert, energetic and not aggressive but fearless. Like most terriers it tends to chase and attack small animals. Stanley Coren ranked it 37th for working intelligence.

Most Airedales need clipping or hand stripping every 6 to 8 weeks, because the coat does not shed in the usual way. As an energetic working terrier, it is generally expected to need daily activity and good training, especially around livestock.

Cancer was the most common cause of death in both a UK and a North American health survey, followed by urologic and cardiac causes and old age. Hip dysplasia is also reported, and the larger Oorang type is said to be more prone to it. A UK study found a life expectancy of 12 years.

faq.q: Why is the Airedale called the King of Terriers?
faq.a: It is traditionally called the King of Terriers because it is the largest of the terrier breeds.
Airedales are described as not shedding much and instead need clipping or hand stripping every 6 to 8 weeks. Their coat is not proven to be hypoallergenic.

faq.q: How long do Airedale Terriers live?
faq.a: They typically live about 12 to 14 years; one UK study found a life expectancy of 12 years.

faq.q: Are Airedales good with other pets?
faq.a: Like most terriers they have a strong instinct to chase small animals, so care is needed with small pets and livestock, especially if the dog is not well trained.
